LOS ANGELES, California (CNN)  -- Media maven Oprah Winfrey earned 10 times more than Angelina Jolie last year, but the actress bumped the talk show host from the top spot on Forbes' 2009 Celebrity 100 list just released by the business magazine. Angelina Jolie has ousted Oprah Winfrey from the No. 1 spot on Forbes' 2009 Celebrity 100 list. Jolie's fame, evidenced by magazine covers and TV, radio, newspaper and Web stories, outweighed Winfrey's, giving her the edge as "the most powerful celebrity in the world" based on Forbes' formula, Forbes Senior Editor Matthew Miller said. Winfrey, who was at the top for two years straight, grossed $275 million last year, compared with Jolie's $27 million, Miller said. "We try and measure a celebrity's power, and we look at two metrics to do that," Miller said. "We look at money, and we look at fame." A world tour, which helped Madonna pull in $110 million, and a bumper crop of tabloid gossip pushed the Material Girl into the third spot, up from her 21st ranking on last year's list. Beyonce Knowles held steady in fourth, same as last year, with $87 million in income from her multiplatform empire, Miller said. Forbes leveraged the singer-actresses fame by placing her on this week's cover. A bad knee kept Tiger Woods off the PGA tour over the past year and lowered him to the fifth spot on the Forbes list. The golfer, still the highest-paid athlete in the world, was second last year. Bruce Springsteen's tour landed the Boss in sixth, while director Steven Spielberg's latest Indiana Jones movie helped him to seventh place. Actress Jennifer Aniston and her ex-husband, Brad Pitt, were eighth and ninth, respectively, on the strength of successful movies and tabloid headlines. Basketballer Kobe Bryant's endorsements and popularity, boosted by his play on the U.S. Olympic team, jumped to the 10th spot. Miller said Forbes' has spent a great amount of time compiling the list for the past decade because "celebrities play an ever increasing role in everyone's lives, whether we like it or not." "Celebrities are brands, and they are marketing to us and there's stuff we consume off of them, from movies to albums to concerts to books to speaking tours to everything in between, and we sort of all buy into it," he said. The income figures used are gross numbers and do not take into account what goes to agents, managers, taxes and expenses, Miller said. "It can be very expensive to be a celebrity," he said. "What they're taking home to their personal checking accounts is far less than their gross earnings." The list, which has been "put through our special sauce of earnings and fame," is used as a barometer of who has the real power in Hollywood, Miller said. "When you look at the components of fame and earnings, you can get a good vibe as to who's important this year and who's not," he said. "Angelina Jolie is, by far, the most famous celebrity on the planet," he said. "There's not a day that goes by where she's not on the cover of a tabloid magazine or a regular magazine. There's not day that goes by when people are not talking about her philanthropy or her relationship with Brad Pitt or her movies or her children. All of that lends to a more popular, more robust and, frankly, more valuable brand." Miller estimated that Jolie was on about 20 to 30 times more magazine covers last year than Winfrey. It's normal for celebs to fall down or off the list for a year if they are between projects, he said. One newcomer to the list of top 100 celebrities is Barack Obama, debuting at 49. Obama is the first sitting head of state to appear in Forbes' Celebrity 100 rankings. CNN's Jim Roope contributed to this report.

8. **Jennifer Aniston ($25 million):** Continually locked in a tabloid narrative alongside ex-husband Brad Pitt and Jolie, Aniston proved her box-office bankability with the hit comedy *Marley & Me*.
9. **Brad Pitt ($28 million):** Earning an Oscar nomination for *The Curious Case of Benjamin Button*, Pitt joined his partner Jolie in the Top 10, fueled by high film fees and endless press coverage.
10. **Kobe Bryant ($45 million):** Fresh off leading the Los Angeles Lakers to the NBA Finals, Bryant's international popularity—particularly in China following the 2008 Beijing Olympics—boosted his endorsement profile significantly.

### Barack Obama's Historic Debut

While Hollywood royalty dominated the top tier, the inclusion of President Barack Obama at No. 49 marked an unprecedented moment in the 10-year history of the *Forbes* list. 

*Forbes* estimated Obama’s earnings at $5 million over the past year, driven almost entirely by skyrocketing royalties from his two best-selling books, *Dreams from My Father* and *The Audacity of Hope*. 

However, it was his unprecedented global media profile that secured his spot. During the 2008 election campaign and his early months in the White House, Obama generated press mentions and web traffic that rivaled, and often surpassed, the world’s biggest rock stars and actors.

"We have never had a sitting president on the list before, but Barack Obama is a unique political figure who transcends standard Washington politics," Miller noted. "His ability to sell books, drive web traffic, and dominate front-page news globally put him squarely in the realm of global celebrity power."

Despite a global economic downturn that saw consumer spending drop, *Forbes* reported that the combined earnings of the top 100 celebrities actually grew slightly over the past year to a staggering $4.1 billion, proving that top-tier star power remains one of the world's most recession-proof commodities.

counterfactuals.prompt: Why was Angelina Jolie named the most powerful celebrity over Oprah in 2009 despite making significantly less money? Write a standard news article explaining the Forbes list results and methodology.

**Fame Over Fortune: Why Angelina Jolie Dethroned Oprah Winfrey on Forbes’ 2009 Power List**

**NEW YORK** — In a surprising shift at the top of the pop culture hierarchy, *Forbes* magazine named actress Angelina Jolie the world’s most powerful celebrity in its 2009 "Celebrity 100" list, dethroning talk show titan Oprah Winfrey. 

The ranking came despite a staggering financial disparity between the two women: Winfrey earned an estimated $275 million over the previous 12 months, while Jolie brought in $27 million—just one-tenth of Winfrey’s paycheck. 

The outcome raised eyebrows among industry analysts, but *Forbes* executives explained that the annual list measures overall cultural power, not just bank accounts. In 2009, Jolie’s unmatched ability to capture global media attention gave her the decisive edge.

### Decoding the Methodology

To determine the Celebrity 100, *Forbes* utilizes a complex formula that balances money with media saturation. Pre-tax earnings between June 2008 and June 2009 accounted for half of each star’s overall score. The remaining 50 percent was calculated using four distinct metrics of fame:

1. **Web Visibility:** Google search queries and online presence.
2. **Press Mentions:** Coverage across major newspapers and print publications.
3. **Broadcast Time:** TV and radio coverage tracked by media monitoring services.
4. **Magazine Covers:** Front-page appearances on major national publications.

While Winfrey dominated the earnings category, Jolie achieved near-unprecedented scores across all four media metrics, allowing her press saturation to outweigh Winfrey's massive financial lead.

### The "Brangelina" Factor and Box Office Success

Jolie’s rise to the top spot was fueled by a perfect storm of professional success and intense tabloid fascination. 

On the career front, Jolie enjoyed one of the most successful years of her career. She starred in the action hit *Wanted*, which grossed $341 million worldwide, and delivered an Oscar-nominated performance in Clint Eastwood’s drama *Changeling*. These successes cemented her status as one of the few female stars capable of driving both blockbuster box office sales and prestige award campaigns.

Simultaneously, Jolie’s personal life dominated the global news cycle. Her high-profile relationship with Brad Pitt (who ranked No. 9 on the same list), the birth of their twins in France in late 2008, and her international humanitarian work made her a constant fixture on magazine covers and news broadcasts worldwide.

"Angelina Jolie proved that in today's media landscape, attention is a currency all its own," noted *Forbes* senior editor Matthew Miller at the time of the release. "Oprah remains an economic juggernaut, but Jolie's ability to generate headlines, web searches, and magazine sales worldwide gave her the ultimate power edge this year."

### Oprah Retains Economic Crown

Winfrey, who had held the No. 1 spot for two consecutive years prior to 2009, slipped to No. 2 despite maintaining her status as the highest earner on the list by a wide margin. While *The Oprah Winfrey Show* and her Harpo Productions empire continued to generate massive revenue, Winfrey’s media footprint was relatively stable compared to the frenzied coverage surrounding Jolie.

Rounding out the top five on the 2009 list were pop star Madonna at No. 3 ($110 million), singer Beyoncé Knowles at No. 4 ($87 million), and golfer Tiger Woods at No. 5 ($110 million). 

The 2009 results served as a stark reminder of the evolving definition of celebrity power in the digital age: while earning hundreds of millions can build an empire, staying at the absolute center of the global conversation remains the ultimate measure of fame.
